scientific_question: At the same certified radius and held-out observations, does a full-covariance denominator ellipsoid produce tighter or looser deterministic prediction bounds than the independent coefficient box?

covariance_rule.source: Use the covariance from the successful attempt with the lowest training residual sum of squares in each frozen fold; extract the denominator block in published parameter order
covariance_rule.validation: Require exact symmetry and positive leading principal minors with rational arithmetic; no covariance refitting or shrinkage
covariance_rule.ellipsoid: Allow denominator perturbations satisfying delta^T Sigma^-1 delta <= rho^2, with the same certified lower radius used by the independent box
covariance_rule.scope: The covariance only defines a deterministic region; it does not create a confidence ellipsoid, probability distribution or physical measurement model

bound_rule.support: At x, compute the exact rational support variance z^T Sigma z and a rational upper bound for its square root, with z=(x,x^2,...)
bound_rule.pointwise_bound: For R=rho*sqrt_upper(z^T Sigma z), require |D|-R>0 and compute |delta f| <= |N|*R/(|D|*(|D|-R)); observed residual bound adds |y-f_snapshot|
bound_rule.comparison: Compute ellipsoid_shift/box_shift only when both are available and box_shift>0; smaller is tighter, larger is looser, no preferred direction is assumed
bound_rule.unavailable: Record non-positive denominator lower bounds and rooted snapshots as unavailable rather than inventing a finite value
bound_rule.scope: Pointwise deterministic bounds only; no continuous-x root-free proof, numerator perturbation or linearized prediction approximation

prohibitions: No covariance refitting, radius retuning or deletion of unfavorable comparisons
No probability, confidence, calibration or physical-measurement interpretation
No claim that an ellipsoid is always tighter or that an unavailable bound is zero
No continuous-x root-free claim from pointwise ellipsoid bounds
